comparison: Perfect agreement on bidirectional functional connectivity between reuniens and mPFC (C3, C25-C38, C70, C78, C80-C81). Both evaluations find the intracellular recording evidence convincing and well-supported, with reviewers explicitly affirming the bi-directional connectivity findings.

Complete agreement on REM sleep findings (C7, C53-C55). Both evaluations support the hippocampal-reuniens coupling during REM, with peer reviewers acknowledging the comprehensive characterization across behavioral states without methodological concerns.

Strong agreement on temporal correlations during oscillatory activity (C39-C46, C68-C69). OpenEval emphasizes statistical rigor while peer reviewers describe this as a 'major finding' with 'convincing evidence.' Peer review additionally includes C4 and C71 in their evaluation, viewing these as part of the broader temporal relationship findings.

Agreement on hippocampal SWR effects on reuniens (C56-C58, C96). Both find the peri-event analysis convincing. Peer review additionally includes C117 in their evaluation, connecting SWR findings to broader spindle timing mechanisms.

Agreement on phase-amplitude coupling and cortical control of timing (C47-C51, C72-C73). Both evaluations support the finding that cortical slow waves precede reuniens and hippocampal events. Peer review additionally includes C5-C6, framing these as part of the broader state-dependent coordination findings.

Agreement on background and motivation claims (C1-C2, C10-C24). Both evaluations accept the anatomical and functional context as well-established. OpenEval separates background claims into R9 (C1, C10-C16) and R10 (C2, C17-C24), while peer review groups all background together.

Agreement that computational model reproduces experimental observations (C59-C62, C123-C126). Both evaluations support the modeling approach. OpenEval separates model validation (R6) from parameter exploration (R7), while peer review groups all computational findings together, including C8 and C63-C67, C127-C131.

Both address computational model parameter exploration (C63-C67, C127-C131). OpenEval notes these are model predictions requiring experimental validation, while peer reviewers accept them as part of the comprehensive modeling approach without distinguishing between validation and prediction phases.

Overlap on background claims (C1, C10-C16). OpenEval separates oscillation background (R9) from anatomical background (R10), while peer review groups all background together. Both find these claims well-supported by prior literature.

Partial overlap on integrative conclusions (C74, C132-C133). OpenEval groups broader integrative claims including C4-C6, C94, C101, C103, C117, C121-C122, while peer review focuses on the reuniens as mediator hypothesis (C9, C74, C132-C133). Both find these conclusions supported by convergent evidence.

Partial overlap on mechanistic interpretations (C103, C121-C122). OpenEval includes these as part of broader integrative conclusions with some caution about inferences beyond direct observation, while peer reviewers accept them as reasonable mechanisms suggested by the data for future testing.

Both address high-level conclusions about reuniens role (C9). OpenEval separates summary statements (R13: C8-C9) from detailed integrative claims (R8), while peer review groups C9 with other mediator role conclusions (C74, C132-C133).

Minimal overlap on modeling conclusions (C8). OpenEval treats C8 as a high-level summary of modeling findings, while peer review includes it with detailed computational results as part of the comprehensive modeling evidence.

Both address the negative finding on SWR-spindle coupling (C52). OpenEval includes this as part of phase-amplitude coupling analysis, noting appropriate reporting of non-significant results. Peer review presents it as part of comprehensive oscillatory coupling analysis without concerns.

OpenEval evaluated background claims on pathway mechanisms and prior research (C75-C77, C79, C82-C93) as supported by citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific background claims.

OpenEval evaluated extensive background on spindle generation mechanisms (C95, C97-C120) as appropriately supported. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, though peer review R9 includes C118 as part of mechanistic interpretations.
OpenEval marked C134 (neuromodulation mechanism) as UNCERTAIN, noting it is speculative and not tested in the study. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this specific claim.

Peer review evaluated C52 (negative SWR-spindle coupling finding) separately as supported. OpenEval included this claim within R3's broader phase-amplitude coupling evaluation rather than as a standalone result.

Peer review grouped mechanistic interpretations (C103, C118, C121-C122) together as novel mechanisms for future testing. OpenEval distributed these across R8 (C103, C121-C122 as integrative conclusions) and R12 (C118 as background), with different framing of their evidential status.
